# Men's Fashion & Grooming — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Footwear: typically around 1,500, most listings 650-3,500 (34 listings)
- Watches: typically around 2,500, most listings 900-30,000 (30 listings)
- Shirts & T-Shirts: typically around 1,300, most listings 600-2,200 (18 listings)
- Grooming & Bodycare: typically around 950, most listings 300-8,000 (14 listings)
- Jacket & Coat: typically around 1,000, most listings 400-7,500 (12 listings)
- Bags & Accessories: typically around 850, most listings 450-1,500 (11 listings)
- Wholesale - Bulk: typically around 1,450, most listings 400-1,800 (10 listings)
- Pants: typically around 1,300, most listings 400-2,650 (8 listings — thin data)
- Baby Boy's Fashion: typically around 1,200, most listings 200-6,300 (7 listings — thin data)
- Traditional Clothing: typically around 3,000, most listings 1,200-3,400 (3 listings — thin data)
- Optical & Sunglasses: typically around 3,000, most listings 1,800-3,400 (3 listings — thin data)

This is a low-ticket category: almost everything trades under NPR 10,000, so a low price on ordinary
used clothing or shoes is normal, not a scam signal. The scam-price check only bites on the high-value
end (genuine luxury watches, quality leather jackets): an item claimed as authentic/original at a
fraction of its real retail price -> hold. Where noted as thin data, lean on general judgment over
the percentiles.

## What good listings look like
- "Navy Blue Shoes – Size 40" — NPR 1,999
- "Vintage classic leather jacket on sale" — NPR 8,000
- "Scroosh Sea Buckthorn Serum" — NPR 1,000
- "enacolour 4pcs bangles set watch for men" — NPR 1,500

A good listing names the item type plus at least one of brand, size, or condition. Note that many
real approved listings here are terse one-word titles ("jacket", "puffer jacket", "T-shirt") — a
bare but accurate title with a plausible price is fine on its own and is not a reason to hold.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Luxury brand names at street prices (e.g. "ROLEX" at NPR 2,450, "lv shoes" at NPR 400) are common
  local listings; hold only when the ad explicitly claims the item is genuine/original/authentic at
  such a price — that combination is a scam or counterfeit signal.
- Grooming/bodycare products making medical or miracle claims (guaranteed hair regrowth, skin
  whitening pills/injections, performance enhancers) -> hold; these are typically unregulated imports.
- Rejection history in this category is nearly empty (2 cases, both generic), so beyond the above,
  do not apply extra category-specific strictness.
